evidence: src/application/task-lookup-service.ts: TaskLookupService.getInProject is the only place that checks `!task || task.projectId !== projectId`.
src/application/assign-task-use-case.ts and src/application/mark-task-done-use-case.ts: both inject TaskLookupService and call lookup.getInProject instead of repeating the check.
src/application/dtos.ts: toTaskDto, toProjectDto and toUserDto are used by every use case to build its result; no use case builds DTOs by hand.
src/application/list-project-tasks-use-case.ts: checks the status filter with the domain's parseTaskStatus instead of doing its own check.

src/application/add-task-use-case.ts and src/application/list-project-tasks-use-case.ts: both repeat the guard `projects.findById` + `throw new NotFoundError(`project ... not found`)`. This minor duplication could become a ProjectLookupService, but it is not a bypassed abstraction.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is one coherent application-service layer: six use-case classes run the project, user and task workflows. Each injects its ports through the constructor, exposes one execute(input) method and returns a DTO. dtos.ts holds all the inputs, outputs and mappers, and task-lookup-service.ts is a shared helper. The rule that a task must belong to the requested project is centralized in TaskLookupService.getInProject. AssignTaskUseCase and MarkTaskDoneUseCase both call it rather than repeating the check. Every use case maps its result through the toXDto mappers in dtos.ts, so nothing builds DTOs by hand. ListProjectTasksUseCase checks the status filter with the domain's parseTaskStatus. The project-existence guard (projects.findById, then throw NotFoundError) appears in both AddTaskUseCase and ListProjectTasksUseCase. It is a three-line guard, not a business invariant, and no existing project-lookup abstraction is being skipped. It could be pulled into a ProjectLookupService to match TaskLookupService, but that is an improvement, not a rubric failure.
